Poseidon did not have a high opinion of Adamas. The two seemed to have a distant relationship, with Poseidon never once looking Adamas in the eye for his entire life until he mutilated him. Poseidon called Adamas pathetic for relying on his army and other Olympians to take down Zeus, and did not hesitate to fight back when Adamas rushed at him. However, Poseidon did have some consideration for his brother, as he chose not to completely kill Adamas and did not mind when Adamas started leading a new life, as Adamantine.
Zeus:
Very little is known about Poseidon's relationship with Zeus. They likely weren't very close, as Zeus did not seem as affected by his death as he was with Hades'. Poseidon respected Zeus' power, as he had no qualms with him ascending to the throne, and did not allow Adamas to threaten his status.
Hermes:
Poseidon was on good terms with Hermes. Despite Hermes' sly behavior, he talked to him casually and asked him to erase Adamas from history. He did not seem to care about Hermes spying on him the entire time or saving Adamas under orders from Hades.

entries.name: Shiva
entries.content:
SPECIES: God
AGE: 4000+
GENDER: Male
PANTHEON: Hindu Pantheon
ORIGIN: Svarga (Heaven)
RELATIVES:
Parvati (First wife)
Kali (Second wife)
Durga (Third wife)
Ganesha (Son)
Shiva is a prominent deity and the leader of the Hindu Pantheon. He is a Chief God and known as the "Cosmos' Bhairava" (宇宙の破壊神バイラヴァ, Uchū no Bairava), the "Strongest God of Destruction" (最強の破壊神, Saikyō no Hakaishin), and the greatest brawler in Heaven.
Appearance:
Shiva is a tall, muscular man shown to have four arms and five golden eyes, with only three of them open when he's calm. He has indigo skin and black hair. He wears a golden bandana and baggy golden trousers equipped with a blue sash. Also, he has blue tattoos on his wrists & fingers, which he had inherited from his best friend, Rudra.
Personality:
Shiva is introduced as a carefree, proud, and powerful God. However, he has shown violent tendencies, even against Zeus himself but stood down in respect of his senior. This is further reinforced when he boldly became shocked by what his opponent thinks of Ragnarok, stating that it is the best event.
In his youth, Shiva was far more lazy and easygoing. Almost every serious thing he did, was through following his best friend, Rudra, while he actually enjoyed to sleep and dance, so much that he wished to become a God of Dancing.
However, he did say he always has fun with Rudra, so he is fine following after him.
Once he and Rudra finished fighting their way to the peak of Svarga, he shows a lot of compassion towards Rudra, trying to change the subject to not fight him and begging Rudra to give up so he wouldn't have to harm him further. In the end, Shiva tried to pretend to act defeated so he could stop the fight and make Rudra happy to think he achieved his dream. However, when Rudra scolded him to give it his all and made him see he really got to the peak of Svarga, he finally accepted the title of leader of their pantheon.
He states in his round that he won't lose to anybody and that he isn't going to let Rudra and the people cheering on him down. Vishnu does comment that Shiva is always reckless while Rudra replies by stating that while he (Shiva) is nicer than anyone, once he get into a fight, he enjoys talking with his fist more than anybody else. Varuna also comments on how Shiva doesn't stop smiling, no matter how many times he gets hit, and Agni states that Shiva doesn't know the meaning of restraint.
Abilities:
Overall Abilities: Shiva is described as being the greatest brawler and strongest god of destruction in all of heaven. He managed to defeat all of the other Hindu gods, including Rudra, who is the second strongest god in the Hindu Pantheon.
Physical Abilities:
Godly Strength: During his battle with Rudra, their clashes sent massive shock waves throughout Svarga and the sound of their punches echoed through the entire land. As said by the other Gods, Shiva has great strength. He managed to grab a punch and a knee from Raiden and send him flying across the arena with his 4 arms, hitting him in the abdomen and making him fall back after the blow. After recovering from Raiden's headbutt, Shiva quickly delivered a barrage of punches with his 4 arms that made Raiden retreat backwards, with the pressure of his punches being compared to cannon fire and causing his opponent several injuries. After having one of his arms crushed, and deciding to fight more seriously, Shiva's punches were able to blow away Raiden, even with his guard up.
Godly Speed ​​& Reflexes: Shiva managed to block Raiden's punch right after being hit hard on the head and also blocked his knee after taking another blow to the head, thus already attacking after defending himself. Shiva, after recovering from Raiden's headbutt, quickly counter attacked with a serie of punches that made Raiden retreat backwards, who had difficulty reacting to all the blows, letting Shiva land one on his head and one on his ribs. After using the Hidden Treasure of Svarga, Shiva's speed increased to the point of leaving multiple afterimages, allowing him to evade Raiden's attacks and overwhelm him with multi-hit attacks.
Godly Durability: According to Shiva, the toughest part of his body is his head, which he claims is solid as rock. Shiva took two full blows from Raiden on the head and quickly recovered after spitting some blood. He endured a headbutt from Raiden, injuring him as a result of their clash.
Godly Endurance & Stamina: Shiva has displayed immense pain tolerance, being capable of staying conscious and continue fighting even after losing three of his arms. During his fight with Rudra, the sweat that flowed from their duel became a heavy rain that rained down upon the entire land, yet despite their fight possibly lasting for hours, Shiva showed no signs of dehydration by the end of it.
Thermal Resistance: Shiva is able to dance until his body starts to generate enough heat to burn the flesh of his opponents. Despite the heat being powerful enough to damage Shiva's own body, he is still able to continue without showing any sings of pain. After using Tandava Karma, Shiva's own body was set on fire and nearby objects started to burn away, yet despite all the damage that he took from this process he was still able to survive the intense heat.
Four Arms: Thanks to his four arms, Shiva possesses far greater dexterity in combat then most people; defending himself from oncoming strikes with one set of arms whilst attacking his opponents with the other pair.
Fighting Abilities:
Master Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Shiva is extremely skilled in the art of unarmed combat. He was able to defeat 1116 Gods with nothing but his fists, including Rudra, his partner that helped him defeat 1115 out of the 1116 Hindu Gods. With his four arms, he can use moves and techniques that can not be performed by most Gods. Even having lost three of his arms, he was still able to fight on par with Raiden.
Expert Dancer: Shiva is also a very skilled dancer, capable of dancing in the rhythm of the cosmos. By implementing dancing in his fighting style, he can fight more effectively and make his movements more unpredictable. He also has multiple techniques which involve dancing and by using said techniques he managed to defeat a great number of powerful gods.
Supernatural Abilities
Semi-Immortality: As a God, Shiva has a limitless lifespan and will not die of old age.
Divine Physiology: As a God, Shiva possesses physical abilities far greater than any ordinary Human. His body cannot be harmed by mortal weapons, however, he can still be harmed by unarmed attacks from individuals with superhuman strength and Divine Weapons.
Pyrokinesis: Shiva can produce powerful heat and flames. The heat is capable of burning nearby objects and turning them into ash, however, he is not completely immune as the heat also harms his body.
Techniques:
Hidden Treasure of the Indian World of Gods (印度神界の秘宝, Indo Shinkai no Hihō) - Known as "Shiva's War Dance" (シヴァの必殺武踊, Shiva no Hissatsu Buyō), this martial dance is Shiva's trump card and can only be performed by him. By dancing to the rhythm of the cosmos, Shiva is able to attack his opponent with far greater speed and power while confusing them. Its unpredictable rhythm allows Shiva to continuously attack his opponent with multi-hit attacks while his opponent is under the impression of being attacked by many, many enemies all at once.
Tandava (Samsara Rebirth) (輪廻武踊ターンダヴァ, Tāndava) - Due to his intense dancing, Shiva's body becomes super-heated and starts to combust, which increases the power of his attacks and burns his opponent.
Krittivasa (Flaming Tiger Claw Dance) (虎爪炎舞クリッティヴァーサス, Kurittivāsasu) - Shiva jumps into the air and brings down a powerful kick while simultaneously combusting his feet, slicing and burning his opponent. The flames created from the kick is hot enough to cauterize the flesh of Raiden, who had Humanity's strongest muscles.
Tandava Karma (Samsara War Dance - Ashes) (輪廻武踊灰塵ターンダヴァ・カルマ, Tāndava Karuma) - Shiva's ultimate secret technique. By forcing his heart to beat faster, Shiva is able to directly stimulate his atman (spirit), resulting in an incredible increase in power and speed. Additionally, his body combust and burns at a higher level than when using Tandava, to the point of burning his surroundings, and objects far away from him to ashes. In this state, all his blows become hot enough to char and burn away flesh and was burning away the powerful muscles of Raiden. There is a drawback to this technique however, as Shiva himself will eventually burn out if he uses the technique for too long.
Deva Loka (Final Act Flame Dance) (大切デーヴァ炎舞ローカ, Dēva Rōka) - A powerful spinning heel kick used by Shiva under his Tandava Karma state. The kick was so powerful and burning hot that it managed to overpower Raiden's most powerful move, Yatagarasu, and rip his arm in half.
Past:
Shiva met Rudra in his childhood, since then, the two remained close. At one point, Rudra asked Shiva what he planned to do in the future. Shiva expressed his desire to become the "King of Dance" with confidence. Rudra, being Shiva's best friend, stated that it's the typical thing for him to do. Rudra proceeded to ask Shiva to promise to not laugh, making it seem like he was about to say something either humorous or important.
Shiva promised, though as Rudra stated that he had a dream, he burst starts bursting out laughing, mocking Rudra for having a dream whilst comparing him to a human. The frustrated Rudra hit Shiva on his head for breaking his promise, before continuing his talk - he uttered that his dream was to stand on top of the gods of India's kingdom. He then asked Shiva whether or not if he wanted to try doing it with him, who then immediately agreed with Rudra's proposal, starting their ultimate journey of seeing the landscape up on the summit of the kingdom; a view yet to be attained by any other gods.
On the way there, many doubted their victory, calling them idiots and inferior gods. However, those words were proven to be mere bluffs as they gradually defeated the gods there. The mockery turned into words of respect, as they continued to advanced through their goal. The more they progressed, the fiercer the fights became and the stronger the gods were. But still, the two defeated them no matter how paramount they were.
Their innumerable gushes of blood finally paid off, they finally eliminated all 1115 gods of the Indian Realm - now, the thing that was left for them to do was to ascend to the peak of Svarga.
Shiva magnified the panorama, calling Rudra to also take a peek at the phenomenon of a view. Rudra, however, notified Shiva that there could only be a single lord at the peak, and not two. Shiva was saddened by the fact, in spite of that, he could not decline reality and decided to brawl with Rudra. The sounds of their fists echoed through India, as their sweats flowed as a heavy rain that covered the land. Despite the tremendous fun they were having, they knew that they both shared the same pain.
After an immensely long amount of time, Rudra started showing signs of exhaustion. This made Shiva pity him, as he begged many times with his wits for Rudra to no longer get up and give up for his own sake. Regardless of that, Rudra had yet to concede defeat and tried to charge towards Shiva and attack him, knowing he'd fail but doing so regardless. As Shiva did not have the will for his dear friend draw his last breath by his own hands, he tried to declare his loss.
Right before he could so, Rudra gave up and admitedt his defeat. Confused, Shiva questioned Rudra, just for him to get shouted at. He started weeping and asked Rudra about his dream, and that he did not want him to abandon it. Rudra encouraged him to not cry, telling him that he is now above 1116 gods. He then asked Shiva if he'd rule over India, to which Shiva said that there was no other way, and accepted the title of the Ruler of Svarga.
Relationships:
Rudra:
Rudra is Shiva's closest friend, the two being together for years. Despite their personalities clashing often, the two held an unbreakable bond. Rudra was the only one Shiva would listen to, and was the reason he ascended to the Top of India to begin with. Rudra and Shiva also seemed to fight well together, the duo being able to demolish anyone in their way, and even besting the stronger Hindu gods like Vishnu and Brahma together.
When they finally reached the top, Rudra forced Shiva to fight him. Shiva cared for his friend so much that he didn't want to fight him, praying for him to fall unconscious before he died fighting. Shiva decided to forfeit, not wanting to hurt his best friend anymore, but Rudra gave up before him. Rudra acknowledged Shiva's power, and told him to be the new leader of the Hindu pantheon. Shiva begrudgingly accepted, and the two parted ways.
Rudra showed up to watch the fifth round of Ragnarok, unbeknownst to Shiva. In Shiva's moment of weakness, Rudra shouted out to his friend, reminding him of his burden and motivating him. Shiva was shocked that Rudra had returned, and with newfound strength defeated Raiden. After the fight he met Rudra in the entrance corridor, collapsing onto him in exhaustion.
Parvati, Kali, Durga and Ganesha:
While he did not directly interact with his wives and son, it can be inferred that he loves them dearly, smiling when he heard their cheers. Parvati, Kali and Durga also came to his room while he was still recovering to keep him company after Round 6, much to his gratitude.
Hindu Pantheon:
Shiva was the leader of the Hindu pantheon, but was also close friends with most of them. He asked them to chant his beat for his war dance, and grew stronger from their cheers. He fought with the pride of the 1116 gods of India inside of him, showing how close he was with them. In particular, Shiva was close with Vishnu, Brahma, Indra, Agni, Varuna and Rudra.
Zeus:
Shiva and Zeus have a rather rocky relationship. Shiva respects Zeus' authority, but will often butt heads with him when their interests clash. During Round 2, when Shiva was preparing to enter, Zeus stopped him. Initially Shiva thought he was there to cheer him on, but Zeus insisted on going instead of him. This enraged Shiva, who wanted to fight Zeus then and there. However, he let Zeus pass out of respect for his status. Shiva also wanted to fight during Round 4, but Zeus declines yet again, wanting payback for Poseidon's death. Shiva was again forced to accept.
After Round 5, Zeus met Shiva in the entrance corridor. The two admitted that humanity was much stronger than they had expected, being back on good terms.

Heracles (Adopted nephew)
Hades wasn't originally listed on the roster, but he volunteered to fill Buddha's spot following his betrayal in the previous round.

He's a prominent deity within the Greek Pantheon, being the "King of the Netherworld" (冥界の王, Meikai no Ō). Hades is also regarded as "The God Whom Other Gods Rely on the Most" (神が最も信頼する神, Kami ga Mottomo Shinrai suru Kami)[
Appearance:
Much like his younger brother, Hades' appearance takes the form of a tall and handsome man with a specially-designed eyepatch on his right eye and long, stylish silver hair that spikes up at various spots on his head.
He's shown with a leaf-like pattern tattooed across his forehead, a spiked choker necklace lined, and a bead-like earring on his left ear with many smaller piercings. His attire is shown to be quite formal and extravagant, with a collar that spans all the way to his upper chest, and badges decorated on the left and right side of his coat. Finally, he wears long white jeans and a pair of shoes filled with square patterns.
Personality:
Hades seems to be a very sophisticated and quiet individual while also being a very respected and feared God among the Greek Pantheon, seen when Ares immediately gives up his seat to him at his order and when all the Gods stood at attention upon him entering the arena.
Hades explains that he helps Beelzebub for his brothers
Hades admits that he loves his brothers very much and misses being with them
Above all else, Hades seems to love all his younger brothers and firmly believes it is his own duty as the eldest to watch over his brothers' backs. Additionally, Hades also believes it is his duty as the eldest to avenge his younger brothers should they ever die, as evidenced by him coming up from Helheim into Valhalla to participate in the seventh round of Ragnarok, all to avenge Poseidon, who died in the third round.
Despite being a king himself, Hades believes that Poseidon was the God most worthy of the title.
Although Poseidon's death was the motivation for him to participate in the Ragnarok tournament, he didn't become blinded by rage and hatred; instead, he remained level-headed and kept his composure since the beginning of his match.
In fact, the only time he lost control of himself was upon discovering that his opponent, Qin Shi Huang, shared a similar view on kingship to that of the late Poseidon, to which Hades' response was to burst out howling with laughter at the irony. He also grew to genuinely respect his opponent's skills as both a warrior and a fellow king. He called the curse that had plagued Qin Shi Huang all his life an unfortunate blight, implying that he would never inflict such a curse on an enemy.
Abilities:
Overall Abilities: As the ruler of Helheim and one of the many possible participants of the Titanomachy and Ragnarok, Hades is incredibly powerful. Like his younger brother, Poseidon, he is a fearsome and dangerous God in his own right, so much so that even other Gods were afraid of invoking his wrath. During the Gigantomachy, Hades defeated an entire army of Titans single handedly.
Physical Abilities:
Godly Strength: Although not as fast as his brothers, Hades makes up for it with being able to unleash a flurry of multiple heavy jabs with his bident that are so strong, it's implied Qin Shi Huang would've died instantly if they'd landed on him. The thrusts of his bident are so powerful that even the wind created from his attacks can slice opponents, which is how he draws first blood against Qin Shi Huang.
Godly Speed ​​& Reflexes: Hades displayed unfathomable movement speed and reaction time, which he can use to enhance his strength, allowing him to buildup a great deal of momentum within his attacks. For example, when Qin Shi Huang's Tortoise Ripple touched the blood on top of his skin, Hades managed to move and shifted the crux of his Qi before the attack could go through the blood completely. His bident techniques are so fast, that they can even create afterimages.
Godly Stamina & Endurance: Hades possesses godly stamina and endurance. He single-handedly wiped out all the Titans that broke free from Tartarus in the Gigantomachy. In his fight with Qin Shi Huang, Hades received many of his own attacks turned back on him, a large portion of his left arm's skin was ripped off and his side was gouged out, yet he remained unfazed. Hades's immense pain tolerance and endurance for blood loss was also demonstrated when he continued to fight on with his chest slashed open by himself and losing lots of blood to feed his bident for its transformation. The bident continued seeping out his blood throughout the fight but Hades seemed to be completely fine with it and was only put down after Qin Shi Huang's final attack had pierced through his heart.
Mental Abilities:
Indomitable Will: Hades has displayed immense willpower. He is regarded as the most reliable God in Heaven, always putting his brothers' well-being over his own safety. He never once showed any signs of fear, even when facing an entire army of Titans by himself.
Keen Intellect: Hades is an extremely intelligent individual. During his fight with Qin Shi Huang, Hades was able to quickly notice the Chinese Emperor's ability to disrupt Qi flow and he was also able to come up with a counter for this ability by covering himself with his own blood to be able to see his attack.
Fighting Abilities
Master Combatant: Hades is shown to possess a great deal of knowledge in regard to combat, as shown when he could predict Buddha's next move against Hajun, proving Zeus, Hermes and Ares wrong. He has more than one millennium worth of experience and was said to have fought in countless battles.
Master Spearman: Hades wields his bident with a godly degree of skill and proficiency, being able to deliver countless blows in the blink of an eye. He also displayed great dexterity in utilizing his bident in combat, delivering powerful blows incessantly and accurately. According to Ares, Hades possesses complete control over his bident.
Supernatural Abilities
Semi-Immortality: As a God, Hades is incapable of dying from old age. He is very ancient, being older than the Big Bang, making him over 13.8 billion years old.
Divine Physiology: As a God, Hades possesses physical abilities far greater than any ordinary Human as well as being impervious to harm by mortal weapons. However, he can still be harmed by unarmed attacks from individuals with superhuman strength and strikes from Divine Weapons.
Matter Manipulation: Hades is able to manipulate objects to an extent as demonstrated when he fused the remains of Poseidon's trident with that of his own bident, creating a newer, more powerful weapon.
Divine Blood: Hades' blood, known as "Pluto Ichor" (プルートイーコール, Purūto Īkōru), is a special substance. Any Divine Weapon that his blood spills upon, will harbor Hades own life force, making them more powerful in the process. He displayed this ability in the Seventh Round when Hades transformed his bident into an even more powerful weapon called "Ichor: Desmos". However, using this ability slowly drains Hades' life force and can result in his death if overused. When Hades used this ability, Qin Shi Huang noticed that Hades' Qi started to flow through his bident, which eventually lead to his downfall.
Techniques:
Persephone Kallichoron (Hammer of the Netherworld) (冥府の銖槌ペルセポネ・カリコロン, Perusepone Karikoron): Hades jumps into the air and jabs his bident down at his opponent. The force is so strong, that it can be carried through the ground and the winds created from the jab could also be used as an form of attack to injure his opponent.
Persephone Roa (Breaker of Storms) (嵐を破壊せし者ペルセポネ・ロア, Perusepone Roa): Hades charges at his opponent and thrusts his bident in a straightforward motion, creating an extremely strong spiral of wind around it as he does.
Persephone Titan (Smasher of Earth) (大地を砕きし者ペルセポネ・ティターン, Perusepone Titān): Hades grips his bident by the polearm near the spearhead and raises it above his own head. From this unusual stance, Hades delivers a mighty downward swing while moving his grip down the polearm, all the way down to the end. He can apply more pressure by gripping the bident with both hands. The force of this attack was able to overwhelm Qin Shi Huang's Heavenly Hand of Defense and crush him into the ground, injuring his head quite a bit.
Cornucopia (Horn of Fertility) (豊穣の角コルヌ・コピア, Korunu Kopia): Hades first swings his bident downwards at his opponent while firmly planting his feet into the ground. As his opponent blocks his bident, Hades proceeds to straighten out his left leg, raise up his right knee and lean back, causing him to knee his opponent's face.
Ichor: Eos (Blood of Dawn) (血が導きし曙光イーコール・エーオース, Īkōru Ēōsu): Hades thrusts Desmos forward while charging at his opponent at the same time. The force of the attack was so strong, that it was able to break through Qin Shi Huang's Almighty Spaulders with ease and grievously injure his left shoulder.
Equipment:
Bident (二叉槍バイデント, Baidento): Hades' personal weapon that consists of two twisted silver prongs, a dark purple-bluish polearm and a silver rounded tip on the other end. Before the seventh round, Hades fused the remains of Poseidon's trident with his bident so he could fight alongside his fallen brother. After doing that, the bident gained a fin-like protrusion.
Ichor: Desmos (Four-Blooded Spear of Destiny) (宿命の四血槍イーコール・デスモズ, Īkōru Desumosu): Hades' trump card. By infusing Pluto Ichor into his bident, Hades upgrades his weapon into Ichor: Desmos, which consists of two sharp prongs with a long blade running through the middle and they all converge into a bloodstained tip. While this version of the bident is powerful, since Pluto Ichor contains Hades' life force, if it were to run out, it would result in his death. The spear is also a living being due to being a part of Hades' body, which means it has a flow of Qi and a crux of Qi is formed with every attack. That is what made it vulnerable to Qin Shi Huang's Tortoise Ripple.
The techniques which Hades used, were named after Greek mythological figures, objects, and concepts:
Persephone was the wife of Hades and the goddess of Spring.
Cornucopia is a horn that produce endless food and nourishment, which belongs to a goddess who protected Zeus when Zeus was still an infant.
Ichor is the blood of the gods and immortals, and became part of ambrosia which Heracles had drank.
Eos is the goddess of dawn.
Gigantomachy:
Following the events of the Titanomachy, Zeus inherited the throne from Kronos and became the new Chief God of the Greek Pantheon, despite being the youngest son. Unable to accept that, the Primordial Goddess, Gaia, led the Giants against the Greek Gods. This conflict would be known as the Gigantomachy.
While the Greek Gods fought against the Giants with all they had, Hades attended a meeting with his brothers, Ares and Hermes. Hermes reported that things weren't looking good and Adamas mockingly asked Zeus what he was going to do, now that he was their Chief God. Both Hades and Poseidon stayed silent. Zeus decided the only thing to do was to pummel the enemy with all their being and headed off for battle. The rest all left through their own exits and Hades sighed after hearing Adamas grumble about Zeus pushing his luck.
As soon as he went through his exit, Hades encountered one of his soldiers and asked what was wrong. The soldier reported to Hades that the Titans, who were subordinates of Kronos, have escaped Tartarus and are planning to invade from Helheim. Poseidon, still around, asked Hades if something was wrong but Hades walked off, assuring his brother he doesn't need to mind.
While the rest of his brothers fought against the Giants, Hades went down into Helheim and confronted the Titans alone. He then fought against them all by himself and was forced to use his trump card. Eventually, after many Titans were slain, the rest retreated and Hades was left sitting atop a broken column, whistling while covered in blood. Soon after, Poseidon arrived and witnessed the bloody scene for himself. Hades assumed Poseidon coming down here means they won the Gigantomachy. Poseidon criticised Hades for being so reckless and going off on his own to face the Titans, leaving his soldiers with them.
Hades insisted that he only did what was right as the elder brother by watching over his brothers' backs. Poseidon brought up that he could've been defeated but Hades said he won't be.
Hades vowed to Poseidon that he will never lose to anyone as the elder brother. Hades then fell back and admitted he may have been a bit too reckless this time around. Scoffing, Poseidon said Hades would hear no thanks from him. He then extended his hand out and called Hades "Brother". That surprised the King of the Netherworld and as he took Poseidon's hand, Hades noted that was the first time Poseidon ever called him his brother.
Fighting the Cursed God:
One day, as he read a book in the king's chamber of his castle, Hades noticed that someone invaded and took out all of his guards. That someone then entered the chamber and Hades remarked on how the intruder being here didn't seem accidental. After putting his book down, Hades identified the intruder as Lord of the Flies, Beelzebub, and questioned him as to what he wanted.
Beelzebub challenged Hades to a fight and Hades recalled hearing a rumor about a reckless fool who fell from Heaven, picking fights with the beasts of Helheim. Since that meant there were no need for words, Beelzebub readied his vibration blade, causing Hades to question if Beelzebub really wants to fight him when he's in such a raggedy state. That led Hades to ask if Beelzebub had a death wish and Beelzebub simply repeated his request. After calling him a troublesome guest, Hades took off his eyepatch and picked up his bident.
He introduced himself as the King of Helheim before he and Beelzebub fought. The only injuries Hades sustained were part of his coat and his right sleeve being ripped before he launched an attack that caused Beelzebub to be sent flying out of the chamber, all the way until the castle walls. As Beelzebub slowly got up, Hades reappeared and Beelzebub praised his strength before crying about this meant he could finally die. This prompted Hades to ask Beelzebub exactly why he wanted to die so badly and Beelzebub showed him by trying to stab himself, only for the tattoo on his chest to stop him.
Beelzebub explained to Hades that he thought the tattoo was a curse given to him by Lilith because he believed she wanted him to live and suffer for killing her. Beelzebub begged Hades to end this curse but Hades immediately pointed out that the tattoo wasn't a curse: it was a prayer. Since Lilith wished for Beelzebub to keep living, Hades instructed him to ask himself how to live rather than how to die. Hades told him to give what he said another thought and as he made his way back into the castle, Hades assured Beelzebub that he'd be waiting for him if Beelzebub still wanted to die.
As he waited for Beelzebub, Hades kept the Staff of Apomyius on him at all times since it suited Beelzebub's abilities.
Some time later, Hades was playing chess with a cockatiel in his chamber when Beelzebub appeared. Hades wondered if Beelzebub wanted to be killed by him and Beelzebub said no. Hades then assumed that he wanted to keep living but Beelzebub said no to that too. Beelzebub divulged to Hades what conclusion he came to: he wanted to live as bitterly, wretchedly, repulsively and savagely just so he can die as horrifically as possible. This initially stunned Hades before he laughed out loud.
Hades sighed about how Beelzebub was such a bothersome fellow before admitting he liked how that sounded.
He then gave him the Staff of Apomyius since Beelzebub won't go down so easily with that before promising to see to Beelzebub's continued suffering and savage demise. Beelzebub asked Hades why he had any concern about him and Hades admitted it was because he was missing his younger brothers, who are quite bothersome, and Beelzebub reminded him of them. As he left, Beelzebub said that Hades was quite a bothersome God himself, much to Hades' confusion.
Adamas' Betrayal:
Upset over how Zeus became the ruler of Heaven, Adamas plotted a rebellion. To help, Adamas freed the remaining Titans and Giants and even bent the grisly Typhon to his will. Adamas also enlisted the help of Hermes, who convinced a number of the other 13 Gods of Olympus to defect, along with 49 members of Zeus' council.
To seal Zeus' fate, Adamas visited Poseidon's palace and tried to convince his younger brother to help him. However, Poseidon was only disappointed and cold-heartedly stated that Adamas defiled everything the Gods stood for. An angered Adamas tried to attack Poseidon but Poseidon grievously injured him with just one thrust of his trident. He then threw Adamas' body aside and left.
Having watched the whole ordeal secretly, Hermes would soon contact Hades and inform him on what happened to Adamas. To save Adamas' life, Hades ordered Hermes to take him to Beelzebub, who proceeded to heal Adamas by reconstructing his body into a cyborg. Since Poseidon had Adamas' name erased from history, he continued to live under a different name, Adamantine, in Helheim.
Relationships:
Poseidon:
Out of all of his brothers, Poseidon seemed to be the one Hades cared the most about. The two had a good relationship, with Hades not minding Poseidon's harsh demeanor and talking to him casually despite his fearsome reputation. He was shocked when Poseidon called him his brother, noting that was the first time he had ever done so.
During Ragnarok, Poseidon's death was the reason Hades left Helheim and came up to Valhalla to join the Gods' roster. Hades merged Poseidon's trident with his own bident and fought Qin Shi Huang in memory of his late brother and the promise he made with him; that he'd never lose to anyone when fighting for his family. Hades' fighting style bore a striking resemblance to Poseidon's, as well as his singing and mannerisms after cutting himself open. Poseidon's outstretched hand was also the last thing Hades saw before his death.
Adamas:
Hades was on good terms with Adamas, despite his wanting to overthrow Zeus. Adamas held great love and respect for Hades, and even felt comfortable working with him in Helheim. While the two never interacted directly in the series, Hades was the one who ordered Hermes to save Adamas, and was the one who contacted Beelzebub to revive him. Hades also apologized to Adamas before his death.
Zeus:
Hades and Zeus had a good relationship, though seemingly not one as close as Hades had with Poseidon. The two got along well and Hades held unconditional love for his youngest brother just like the rest of his family. Hades apologized to Zeus before his death.
Beelzebub:
Hades was good friends with Beelzebub. Despite the latter's fearsome reputation and murdering of his friends, Hades still pitied him and decided to help Beelzebub live a fulfilling life. He initially listened to Beelzebub's request to kill him, but before delivering the final blow, he decided against it after hearing about Lilith's curse. He urged Beelzebub to search himself for the meaning of her prayer, and that if he still wanted to die, he would be waiting. When Beelzebub eventually did return, Hades was amused by his new approach to life: to live as horribly and corruptly as possible so that he would receive an equally painful death. He provided Beelzebub with the Staff of Apomyius, hoping that the now much stronger Beelzebub would have a much harder time dying. When asked by Beelzebub why he cared about him so much, Hades stated that he had three bothersome younger brothers, and just when he began to miss them, Beelzebub had wandered into his palace.
Hades outlawed the use of Original Sin of the Netherworld — No. 0: Chaos, due to the destruction it caused and due to the effects it had on Beelzebub. When Adamas was gravely injured by Poseidon, Hades contacted Beelzebub to save his brother, showing the trust he had in him. Hades' death also had a large impact on Beelzebub, as he'd been his only friend after his other friends and lover were killed by his Demonic Destrudo.
Ares and Hermes:
Hades was on good terms with Ares and Hermes. He interacted very little with Hermes, but he seemed to tolerate him and value his presence. Hades often made fun of Ares, and seemed to scare the God of War too. However, Ares still looked up to his uncle and found him to be the most reliable God.

entries.name: Apollo
entries.content:
Apollo is a prominent deity within the Greek Pantheon. He is known as the "Sun God" (太陽神, Taiyō-Shin) and is a part of the Twelve Gods of Olympus. He is also known by the title of "Phoebus" (ポイボス, Poibosu) and is considered to be the "Boxing God" (ボクシングの神, Bokushingu no Kami).
Through his own effort, Apollo has earned himself a number of distinguished titles, such as the "God of Philosophy" (哲学の神, Tetsugaku no Kami), the "God of Poetry" (詩歌の神, Shiika no Kami), the "God of Medicine" (医学の神, Igaku no Kami), the "God of Archery" (弓の神, Yumi no Kami), the "God of Music" (音楽の神, Ongaku no Kami) and the "God of Prophecy" (予言の神, Yogen no Kami), being praised as the most talented God.
SPECIES: God
AGE: Eons
GENDER: Male
PANTHEON: Greek Pantheon
ORIGIN: Unknown (Heaven, possibly)
RELATIVES: Artemis (Twin sister)
Zeus(father)
Appearance:
Apollo is an attractive man with flowing long light pink hair that reaches down to his torso and a body of good physique.
Like many of the Gods of the Greek Pantheon, he wears items related to Greece such as a laurel wreath, buskin sandals and toga. The toga though has elements of clothing more akin to a kimono such a sash around his torso (Obi) and flower designs on the outside of the chest area with it being opened to show his chest. He is decorated with jewelry with him wearing a necklace extending down his chest that resemble the sun and its rays, a chain that is a part of his sash and a decorated chain around his right leg. Underneath his Divine Weapon, he wears black gloves that only cover his thumbs, index and middle fingers, leaving his ring fingers and pinkies, and the area around them, exposed.
Personality:
Apollo appears to be an extremely narcissistic individual, who cares a lot about beauty, when it comes to himself and even others. When he had heard news of the deaths of other Greek Gods in Ragnarok, his first reaction wasn't to mourn them but rather, wish he could've been there to see their deaths as they must've looked beautiful when they died. In addition to being narcissistic, Apollo looks down on anyone who doesn't fit his own standards of what is beautiful. This is especially in the case of Humans such as at the start of the ninth round: when Leonidas leapt in before Heimdall could even finish saying "Fight!", Apollo criticised him for being like a wild beast, considering him less than a Human.
Apollo's narcissistic nature has also made him have a flare for the dramatic, always doing grandiose and expressive poses. This was first demonstrated when he was in the bath and posing for each grand line, not caring if he was nude or not. This did not dim down in battle, with him outright mocking Leonidas with his expressions, words and poses.
Apollo strongly believes that what makes a person beautiful is not what their outward appearance looks like – it's whether or not that person truly knows themself. He thinks that those aren't beautiful are those who rest on the laurels of their good fortune and do nothing more while those that are beautiful are those who know their own weaknesses and don't fear changing themselves.
Abilities:
Overall Abilities: Narcissism aside, Apollo is a formidable God in combat, thanks to his extreme reflexes and speed that make him nearly impossible to hit. Combined with his natural talent in boxing, Apollo can counter any attack without losing momentum or breath. So much so, he could put fighters like Leonidas on the ropes where even Leonidas' Völundr could not surprise the God enough to let his guard completely down.
Physical Abilities:
Godly Speed & Reflexes: Apollo had demonstrated not only speed to that of a God or Human fighter, but possibly speed that surpasses others. This was demonstrated when an angry Ares, the God of War, tried to slug the Sun God for his insolence while he was in the nude, with Apollo effortlessly dodging and even throwing the God of War into the water. Apollo can even quickly adapt to sudden attacks, with him able to dodge many of Leonidas' surprise attacks despite never seeing them until that moment.
Godly Endurance & Stamina: Apollo has great resistance and can withstand very strong and painful blows. When Leonidas managed to hit Apollo with Phalanx Nemesis, he received the blow directly to his face and hit the ground so hard that he bounced off it and fell back to the ground face-first. Although it took him a while to get up, it didn't take him long, and his reaction was one of happiness and joy, fully accepting the unsightly wound on his face with pride.
Mental Abilities:
Self-Knowledge: Apollo was born as an ordinary and mediocre god, but thanks to his desire to be better, he managed to achieve all his titles, skills and competencies through pure hard work and effort. His knowledge of himself led him to improve and become one of the 12 Gods of Olympus. He is the first natural God who has accepted that he is weak and strived to be the strongest.
Fighting Abilities:
Master Boxer: Apollo has shown immense skill in boxing, evident by his ability to dodge Leonidas' quick attacks, while also being able to quickly strike back.
Master Archer: Apollo has been classified as a very skilled archer, during his life he has trained and practiced a lot to become "God of Archery", in addition to that he himself has been able to kill several Giants, and destroy the defenses of Argos during the Gigantomachy, and also for the fact of wounding Leonidas numerous times.
Supernatural Abilities:
Semi-immortality: As a God, Apollo is incapable of dying due to old age.
Divine Physiology: As a God, Apollo possesses physical abilities far greater than any ordinary Human. His body cannot be harmed by mortal weapons; however, he can still be harmed by unarmed attacks from individuals with superhuman strength and Divine Weapons.
Photokinesis: As the God of the Sun, Apollo can produce and control light. He can manipulate and craft the light into fine and durable threads for combat that can block Volundr-level attacks with ease.
Matter Manipulation: Thanks to his threads of light that he can create, Apollo can manipulate and weave them to create any weapon or object he needs. This will open up an infinite number of possibilities such as a Shield, a Lyre, Boxing Gloves, a Bow, etc.
Expectations-Induced Enhancement: Apollo can enhance his physical, mental and supernatural abilities based on the expectations and criticism of others, whether allies or enemies. This was seen when he activated his strongest form because of all the comments from the stands. It is a power that Zeus himself cannot define, since it is not tied to any type of logic or common sense. The more the public's emotion, the more affinity Apolo will have.
Techniques:
Phoebus' Lyre (The Shimmering Harp) (光輝きて堅琴ポイボス・ライアー, Poibosu Raiā): Apollo creates a pair of hands out of his threads and places his own hands into them, which transforms the Threads of Artemis into a pair of boxing bracers with pronounced wristbands and studded knuckles. These pair of bracers enhance Apollo's close-range boxing abilities.
The Sun Shall Never Set on Me (Embrace of the Eternal Midnight Sun) (白夜の抱擁オレ様という太陽は沈まない, Oresama to iu Taiyō wa Shizumanai): Apollo's strongest battle mode. A power that defies all logic and common sense, Apollo can actually get stronger the more that he lives up to the expectations of those around him, whether they be an ally or an enemy. When this happens, Apollo emits a large amount of light from his body.
Artemis Elenchos (Shining Domination) (光り輝く支配アルテミス・エレンコス, Arutemisu Erenkosu): Apollo wraps his threads around his opponent's limb to immobilise their movement.
Apollo Epicurious (Golden Arrows of the Shining Meteor) (輝ける流星の黄金矢アポロン・エピクリオス, Aporon Epikuriosu): Apollo launches a large wave of his light arrows at his opponent to overwhelm them.
Argyrotoxos (Soul-Piercing Silver Arrow) (魂を射抜し銀矢アリュギュロトクソス, Aryugyurotokusosu): If Apollo cannot draw his bow anymore, he can give the bow back to the statue. The statue will then deform the bow back into threads and form a very thick rope between its hands. Afterwards, the statue drops its hands to the ground and Apollo leans back on the rope while digging his feet really hard into the ground, drawing himself back like an arrow. Once he pulls his right fist back in preparation for a punch, Apollo lifts his feet up from the ground and is sent flying towards his opponent. While flying forward, Apollo's right fist hardens the light energy that is around it, creating an arrow covering it. This attack was powerful enough to destroy Leonidas' Völundr and deal a fatal blow through his body in the final moments of Round 9, though the arrow was broken on impact with the shield.
Equipment:
Threads of Artemis (アルテミスの糸, Arutemisu no Ito): A set of golden gauntlets with a dark blue underside, three small studs on each knuckle, and small holes above each fingertip. Upon Apollo producing light from his fingertips, they transform into threads that he can use for defensive or offensive purposes.
Moonlight of Artemis (アルテミスの月影, Arutemisu no Tsukikage): Apollo's Threads of Artemis disappear from his hands and right after, a large shadow extends out behind him. A giant statue of Artemis then appears from the shadow, equipped with Apollo's Divine Weapon. The statue weaves the threads it produces to make a giant golden bow, its length being twice as tall as Apollo is. Apollo can use the bow to fire arrows of light, that are invisible when fired because they move at light speed. Because of how fast the arrows are, they are known as the fastest attack in Valhalla and Zeus believes no-one other than himself can defend against them.
Gigantomachy:
Along with all the other Greek Gods, Apollo took part in the Gigantomachy against Gaia and the Giants. It is noted by Hermes that this war was the last time Apollo shined greatly before the ninth round of Ragnarok. Zeus has stated that Apollo used his golden bow against the Giants during this war and that the Giants could do nothing against his arrows of light.
During the time of Ancient Greece on Earth, a serpent-like monster called Python was driven out of Valhalla for his hideous appearance. Shunned by the Humans as well, Python took out his frustration on them by constantly terrorizing the village of Delphi. During one of his rampages, Ares sent his Divine Honor Guard to stop him but Python easily dealt with them. After hearing of this, the next day, Apollo went down to Earth and confronted Python at his hideout, wanting to meet Ares' expectations by defeating Python by himself, though Ares never asked him to.
Python was excited to see Apollo as he perceived the God to be the complete opposite of himself. Thus, Python wanted to rip his face to shreds. Python charged forward but Apollo leapt in and punched Python squarely in the face. Apollo decided this was his win and Python found himself unable to get up, from just one punch. Not wanting to give up, Python shouted about how he hasn't lost yet and Apollo found that attitude great, telling Python that they shall continue their fight tomorrow. Apollo went to sleep in Python's bed and ordered him to find somewhere else to sleep.
For the next several days, Apollo fought Python, defeating him in one punch every time. During one rainy day, Apollo got curious and asked Python why he continued to fight him. Python divulged to Apollo how he was despised and oppressed because of an appearance he didn't even ask for. The serpent cried and insisted that he couldn't stomach the thought of losing to Apollo, who seemed to have been blessed with everything from birth. When Python expressed his unwillingness to give up, Apollo said he was beautiful.[9] Python thought Apollo was making fun of him but Apollo clarified that he wasn't referring to Python's appearance; rather he found Python's soul beautiful.
He explained to Python that he could understand him because he was the same. Apollo was originally a mediocre God but he worked hard and became recognized through effort alone, to the point where he was able to join the ranks of the Twelve Gods of Olympus. Apollo told Python that the ones who aren't beautiful to him are those who are satisfied with where they are while those who are beautiful, are those who know they aren't enough and don't fear changing themselves for the better. Finally understanding, Python then began crying over how he'd hurt so many people, but Apollo didn't hold it against him as he was just defending himself. Apollo decided to go back to Valhalla and Python shouted about how he still hasn't lost, causing Apollo to remark on how that's beauty.
After Apollo left, Python stopped terrorizing Delphi and instead, built a temple dedicated to Apollo, engraving it with the words, "Know Thyself."

entries.name: Ragnarok
entries.content:
Ragnarok  is Mankind's final struggle against the Gods. Explained in the Valhalla Constitution, article No. 62, paragraph 15 of the "super special clause," it is a series of one-on-one showdowns between the Gods and Mankind.

The rules are quite simple. Each side picks thirteen fighters, who will fight one-on-one fights to the death and the winning side is the one that gets seven victories first.

If the Gods win the Ragnarok, Humanity's fate is sealed and it will be extinguished. However, if the Humans win, they will gain the right to live for another 1000 years.

As Ragnarok is a battle between souls, those who die in the fights have their souls destroyed and turned to ashes, being impossible to save or retrieve the soul, this impedes the reincarnation cycle, therefore, resulting in complete extinction.
The fights take place in the Valhalla Arena.
Loopholes:
As the super special clause was originally added as a joke in the Valhalla Constitution and never meant to be taken seriously, it created loopholes that both teams took advantage or might take advantage of:

While it's stated that only the fighters and the commentartor can enter the arena, if a new entity appears but it's considered part of the original fighter's body, a long time animal companion for example, it can be allowed to stay and even assist the fighter.
The teams can switch out their representatives for another, even at the last minute before a round begins.
It's possible for a team to know which fighter the other team picked before announcing their own.
There is no restriction on which species should the participants be. Meaning Gods can fight for Humanity, or Demigods and Demons for the Gods.
A fighter can switch teams should he wants to.
A fighter can fight more than once.
Should anything happen to a fighter prior to their fight, their team is allowed to have a replacement.
Trivia:
In Norse mythology, Ragnarök is a series of events, including a great battle, foretold to lead to the death of a number of great figures (including the gods Odin, Thor, Týr, Freyr, Heimdallr, and Loki), natural disasters and the submersion of the world in water. After these events, the world will resurface anew and fertile, the surviving and returning gods will meet and the world will be repopulated by two human survivors. Ragnarök is an important event in Norse mythology and has been the subject of scholarly discourse and theory in the history of Germanic studies.

entries.name: Gods' Council
entries.content:
The Gods' Council is an event that happens once per millennium in which the Gods of every pantheon decide Humanity's fate by the process of voting.
The Gods decide if Humanity should continue to exist through a collection of votes. If the majority of votes are against Humanity then that means their existence must come to an end, though they may cancel the result of the vote by winning in Ragnarok.

If the decision for mankind's destruction is not agreed upon by the majority, the Gods may choose to punish Humanity by destroying key elements of civilization.
Zeus is the current chairman of the Council.
Plot:
Around 4000 years ago, Zeus chaired the Gods' Council to decide Humanity's fate. In the end, they allowed Humans to keep on living but not without punishment.

Aphrodite suggested the destruction of the city of Thebes and Shiva offers to go there personally, but Ares intervenes asking if he can be the one to punish Thebes by being part of his jurisdiction.
Trivia
It appears that Demigods are not allowed to vote in the council, since none of the Valkyries were seen voting. However, it is possible that the gods do allow some exceptions, such as in the case of Heracles, due to him being a very powerful individual and an adopted son of Zeus.

entries.name: Titanomachy Tournament
entries.content:
The Titanomachy Tournament  was a tournament that took place eons ago between the Gods and the Titans to decide which side will reign supreme.
The Titanomachy Tournament took place somewhere in the Milky Way and, unlike Ragnarok, it seemed to include preliminaries.

The tournament was created in order to decide which side would rule over the universe, the Gods or the Titans. The Gods were victorious and Zeus became their leader. Meanwhile, the remaining Titans were imprisoned in Tartarus.
Trivia:
In Greek mythology, the Titanomachy was a ten-year series of battles fought in Thessaly, consisting of most of the Titans (an older generation of gods, based on Mount Othrys) fighting against the Olympians (the younger generations, who would come to reign on Mount Olympus) and their allies. This event is also known as the War of the Titans, Battle of the Titans, Battle of the Gods, or just the Titan War. The war was fought to decide which generation of gods would have dominion over the universe; it ended in victory for the Olympian gods.

entries.name: Gigantomachy
entries.content:
The Gigantomachy  was a war between the Greek Gods and the Giants, who were being led by Gaia.
The root cause of this war is the result of the Titanomachy Tournament between the Titans and the Gods. In the final round of the Titanomachy, Zeus defeated his father, Kronos. Thus, he took Kronos' place and became Chief God over all Greek Gods. Unable to accept that outcome, the Primordial Goddess, Gaia started a war against the Greek Realm and led her spawn, the Giants. That is what is known as the Gigantomachy.

In the final moments of the Gigantomachy, Zeus led the Greek Gods against the Giants and won. What happened to Gaia is unknown. At the same time as Zeus led the Greek Gods into battle, the Titans broke out of Tartarus and begun to advance to Valhalla from Helheim to assist the Giants. However, they were single-handedly repelled by Hades.
Trivia:
The Gigantomachy was probably the most important battle that happened in Greek mythology. It was a fight between the Giants or Gigantes, sons of Gaea and Uranus, and the Olympian gods who were trying to overthrow the old religion and establish themselves as the new rulers of the cosmos.

entries.name: Niflhel
entries.content:
Niflhel  is the term often used in "Shuumatsu no Valkyrie: Record of Ragnarok" instead of the word "oblivion".
It is the fate of all who lose and die during Ragnarok.
Overview:
In the universe of Shuumatsu no Valkyrie, going to Niflhel means having your soul destroyed, which prevents reincarnation, and having your body reduced to dust in the vacuum of space.
It is believed that this process is irreversible, being seen as a form of permanent death and that once someone is send to Niflhel they will never been seen again.
Demons, gods and other supernatural creatures are sent to Niflhel automatically when they die, while humans go to Heaven after death. However, if a human dies in the afterlife they will be sent to Niflhel.

entries.name: Valhalla
entries.content:
Valhalla, also known as Heaven, is one of the three main worlds of "Shuumatsu no Valkyrie: Record of Ragnarok" (alongside Midgard and Helheim). It's the world where the Gods and the souls of the dead dwell. While Gods are native to Valhalla, Human souls are guided there by the Valkyries.
Valhalla is currently ruled by the Supreme Greek God, Zeus.
Eons ago, the Titans and the Gods fought against each other. They held the Titanomachy tournament in order to decide which of the two species would reign supreme. During this tournament, Zeus would kill his own father Kronos, becoming the new ruler of Heaven as a consequence.

At some point, there was a war between Heaven and Hell. After the war, a gate known as the Bifröst was built in order to prevent an invasion from either side.

Fitting of its name, Valhalla is a place filled with surreal beauty. Most places in Valhalla have a beautiful landscape with clean rivers and a clear blue sky. Other places also have unnatural structures, such as flying castle-like objects.

entries.name: Valhalla Arena
entries.content:
The Valhalla Arena  is the location where all the battles of Ragnarok take place.
The Valhalla Arena changes appearance in almost every round of Ragnarok. The arena's exact size is unknown and little is known about what it is comprised of either. The Arena exists somewhere within the Gods' Realm. The Valhalla Arena can be divided into two sides: Humanity's side and the Gods' side. In each round, the people who are associated with the participants are allowed to sit in the front rows of the arena.

entries.name: Asgard
entries.content:
Asgard is one of the nine realms in Norse mythology and is the home and fortress of the Aesir gods.
In the ancient era, giants of Jötunheim launched an offensive on Asgard. Over centuries, the warriors of Asgard became overconfident and their battle experience dwindled until their defenses had waned. Asgard had been brought to the edge of destruction, with many warriors and citizens killed and eaten by the giants. When it seemed like all hope was lost, Thor confronted them and wiped out the entire army of 66 Jötnar by himself.
RULER(: Odin
LOCATION: Valhalla
INHABITANTS: Norse Gods, Angels Guards
Asgard is a city surrounded by a wall with an enormous tree at its center. The city is located on top of a mountain and can only be accessed after climbing a flight of stairs and walking through a giant gate.

The architecture of the city is similar from that of medieval towns, with most houses only having one or two floors at most.

entries.name: Garden of Eden
entries.content:
The Garden of Eden was an idyllic garden where Adam and Eve resided before being expelled to Earth.

Approximately 7 million years before Ragnarok, Adam and Eve lived in the Garden of Eden alongside other fellow creations.

That was until the Serpent falsely accused Eve of eating an apple from the Tree of Knowledge. Despite the evidence having been clearly forged, the heavenly court of justice, which consisted entirely of gods, ruled Eve guilty. When she was about to be expelled from the Garden, Adam broke into the courtroom with two baskets full of the forbidden fruit and took a bite out of all of them so he would be expelled from the Garden of Eden along with his wife.

Later Lucifer and his friends would hang out on Eden and steal apples from its trees, eventually Beelzebub would join them as well.

The Garden of Eden is a place of divine and ethereal beauty. It is a flat landscape with mountains surrounding it. It contains a great variety of animals and insects all of which live in harmony, despite some of them being carnivores. Eden is located at one of the many flying islands that exist within Heaven.

Tree of Knowledge:
The garden of Eden possess a tree which contains the forbidden fruit, an apple which its consumption is considered a divine crime. All humans that eat this fruit are banished from Eden. Even though eating this apple is considered a severe crime, the reasons for it are never explained.

Heaven's Court:
Within the land of the Gods, the gods are responsible for the judgement and punishment of criminals. However, despite Eden having prosecutors and judges, the chances of a human receiving a guilty verdict is 99.99999%. For that reason, its not very difficult to convict a human by using forged evidence.

Trivia:
Before the Fifth Round of Ragnarok, several sponsor banners were paraded around the ring. One of these banners was an advertisment for an establishment called "Seriously Tasty - Garden of Eden". The establishment appears to be a restaurant.

entries.name: Svarga
entries.content:
Svarga is the land from which all the Hindu gods originate.
RULER(S): Shiva
LOCATION: Valhalla
INHABITANTS: Hindu Gods
The Svarga is a group of mountains located in India, and among those mountains there is one that is the largest to the point where it reaches the clouds and where you can see almost all of India
Long ago, the realms of Svarga and Patala were filled with thousands of gods.
Shiva becomes the leader of the Hindu Pantheon anime
Although many tried, not a single deva had managed to climb to the top of Svarga and unify the Hindu gods under their rule, until Shiva and Rudra went of a journey to defeat the 1115 gods of India. They defeated all of their opponents, from asuras to Brahma and Vishnu, and found themselves at the peak. However, for the good of both gods and mankind, Shiva and Rudra had to fight for the title of the supreme Hindu god. Shiva ended up winning and becoming the leader of the Hindu pantheon.

entries.name: Olympus Palace
entries.content:
The Olympus Palace is the home base of the Twelve Olympians.
RULER(S): Zeus
LOCATION: Valhalla
INHABITANTS: Twelve Gods of Olympus, Warrior Angels, Maids
During the Gigantomachy, the Olympus Palace acted as a stronghold and meeting place for the Greek Gods to heal their wounds and discuss the situation.
It is a large palace located in Valhalla, where the Greek Gods live like the Twelve Gods of Olympus and are led by Zeus, in addition to there are also servants and the divine vanguard of the Angels.
Finally they have a meeting room composed of a round table, where several Greek Gods such as Zeus, Hades, Poseidon, Adamas, Ares and Hermes meet.

entries.name: Midgard
entries.content:
Midgard is one of the three main worlds of "Shuumatsu no Valkyrie: Record of Ragnarok" (alongside Valhalla and Helheim). It's the place where Humanity and animals live.
ALIASES: Earth
RULER(S): Various
INHABITANTS: Humans, Animals
Approximately 7 million years before Ragnarok, Adam and Eve descended to Earth after being expelled from the Garden of Eden. The two of them became originators of the Human race.
Recently, a lot of the natural environment in Midgard has been destroyed due to Humanity's actions. For example, the seas are filled with waste and oil, many of its forests are gone and many other species living on Midgard have gone extinct or are endangered. This ended up making many Gods, such as Aphrodite, desire the extinction of mankind.
Midgard looks identical to its real world counterpart, possessing a great variety of landscapes (from cities to forests). A great deal of its natural environment has been affected due to pollution and deforestation caused by Humanity, this being one of the main reasons why the Gods desire humankind's extinction.

entries.name: Savage Land
entries.content:
The Savage Land is a lawless land where Dong Zhuo was born.
Somewhere in a place unbeknownst to anyone, individuals discarded by the world had gathered together. They were criminals, slaves and members from the lower class from all over the globe. They came from the Han Empire, the Satavahana Dynasty, the Kushan Dynasty, the Parthian Empire and even from the Roman Empire.
The Savage Land is a place surrounded by mountains. It has little to no vegetation and is full of human bones and rotten flesh.
Political System:
There are no concepts of origin or hierarchy in the Savage land. There are also no oficial laws, being a place where the strong rule.
Rubbish Bazaar & Economic System:
The Rubbish Bazaar is a commercial area that can be found in the Savage Land. There, people can exchange goods through trade, instead of using money.

entries.name: Helheim
entries.content:
Helheim, also known as the Netherworld or just Hell, is one of the three main worlds of "Shuumatsu no Valkyrie: Record of Ragnarok" (alongside Valhalla and Midgard). It's the world where Demons and other unearthly beings dwell.
Helheim was previously ruled over by Hades, who was defeated in the seventh round of Ragnarok. Some other Gods, such as Beelzebub, also seem to live in this realm. Currently, there is no ruler.
ALIASES: The Netherworld, Hell
RULER(S): Hades 
INHABITANTS:Hades ,Beelzebub,Adamantine,Cerberus ,Siegfried,Demons,Titans
Many eons ago, Helheim was left half-destroyed by Hajun before disappearing and then resurfacing during Ragnarok.
At some point, there was a war between Heaven and Hell. After the war, a gate known as the Bifröst was built in order to prevent an invasion from either side.
After the Titanomachy Tournament, Hades became the ruler of Helheim. This was done so that he could supervise the demons in order to prevent them from causing any trouble in the Netherworld or going up to Midgard and causing chaos.
During this time, the Titans were also imprisoned in Tartarus. However, they were freed by Adamas later.
After trying to overthrow Zeus, Adamantine, formerly known as Adamas, was forced to work for Hades in hell.
Description:
Fitting of its name, Helheim is an ominous and hostile environment. It has little to no vegetation and it is filled with mountains. The sky is also mostly dark and cloudy, making it even more difficult to grow food and plants.

entries.name: Tartarus
entries.content:
Tartarus, also known as the Pits of Tartarus and the Prison of the Gods, is a place in Hell that is used as a prison for the Titans, the Demons and Siegfried.
LOCATION: Helheim
INHABITANTS: Siegfried, Demons, Titans
After the Titanomachy Tournament, the remaining Titans were imprisoned in the pits of Tartarus.
During the Gigantomachy, the Titans escaped from Tartarus and Hades decided to fight them on his lonesome, successfully repelling all of them using the power of his Ichor: Desmos.
However, they would eventually be freed by Adamas and would aid him in his attempt to overthrow Zeus. After Adamas' "death" at the hands of Poseidon, it is unknown what happened to the Titans.
At some point in time, Siegfried was imprisoned in Tartarus.

entries.name: Humans
entries.content:
Humans are one of the existing species in the world. They are beings that were created by the Gods.
RULER: Various
LOCATION: Earth, Heaven
Humans are native to Midgard and can be usually be found there. However, since the souls of the dead are brought to Valhalla by the Valkyries, they can also be found within Heaven. Humans can also be send to Hell if they break the laws of the Gods.
As beings created in the image of the Gods, Humans have a very similar appearance to their creators.
The current details of Humanity’s origins are not fully clear, but at one point (about 7,000,000 years before Ragnarok) in the Land of the Gods, one deity created two beings in his image to populate the Earth and rule over the animals, whom he named Adam and Eve. Sometime after this, a demon framed Eve as revenge for turning down his advances. In court, he falsely accused her of eating fruit from the Tree of Knowledge. Eve was ruled guilty and banished from the Garden of Eden, and Adam decided to go with her. After leaving Heaven and going to Earth, Adam and Eve would live there and have many children, such as Cain and Abel.
From that point on, Humanity's history is almost identical to what is known in real life from historical science, as well as from various myths and religions.
Humanity's culture is identical to real life, varying greatly depending on the location and time period. The same can be said about their laws and social structure.
Golden Age: Once a Human soul arrives at the afterlife, they will have the appearance that they had during their golden age: the age in which they were at their peak. This usually results in most Human souls permanently having a youthful appearance and a healthy body.
Superhuman Physiology: Whilst most Humans have very inferior physical abilities when compared to those of a God, some exceptional individuals have the power to compete against their creators. Some Humans also have unique abilities, either through divine intervention (like Adam), through a rare medical condition (like Raiden Tameemon) or through other methods.
Ascension to Godhood:
It is possible for a Human to become a God. This can be done through a variety of methods, such as drinking the Ambrosia (like Heracles) or by reaching enlightenment (like Buddha).
Gods
During ancient times, Humanity and the Gods had a close relationship, having a great number of worshippers in each pantheon who used to pray every day to praise the Gods. Whenever the Gods were displeased with Humanity's actions, they would cause catastrophic events to happen, such as the destruction of the Tower of Babel. This practice was stopped at the request of Alcides when he became a God.
The connection between Humans and the Gods slowly grew weaker as time passed, until in the 21st century, the Gods condemned the species to extinction for their immoral behavior and destruction of the environment. To prevent this, Brunhilde convinced the Gods to use Ragnarok to determine Humanity's fate.
No manmade weapons can harm the Gods, however, unarmed attacks by individuals with superhuman strength can still harm them.
Demons:
Not much is known about the relationship between mankind and demonkind. However, from what is known about Human culture and folklore, Humans think that demons are evil beings that must be feared. In the past, Chiyou managed to leave Helheim and go to Earth, becoming an evil tyrant who ruled over China until he was killed by Qin Shi Huang.

entries.name: Gods
entries.content:
Gods are one of the existing species in the world. They are the creators of Humanity and decide the fate of the world.
RULER: Zeus
LOCATION: Heaven
Most Gods can be found within Heaven, with a few notable exceptions, such as Hades, who rules over and resides in Helheim as its king.
Many Gods have a very humanoid appearance, being very similar to that of a Human. However, there are many other Gods that either have in-human traits such as multiple eyes or horns, to being outright beastfolk such as snakes or birds.
The origin of the Gods is currently unknown, but what is known is that at some point, the Titanomachy Tournament occurred, in which the Gods fought against Titans. The Gods were victorious and Zeus became leader of the Greek Gods after killing his father, Kronos. Zeus becoming leader of the Greek Gods greatly upset the Primordial Goddess, Gaia, who led the Giants in a war against the Greek Gods in a battle known as the Gigantomachy. The Greek Gods were victorious and what became of Gaia is unknown. Some time after the Gigantomachy, Zeus became the leader of all of Heaven.
culture:
While the intricacies of their culture are unknown, what is known is that the Gods focus and pay respect to strength. For instance, Shiva became the leader of the Hindu Pantheon by challenging and defeating all the other Hindu Gods in battle. Another example can be seen with Zeus, who despite being the youngest of his brothers, became the King of Olympus after defeating his father, Kronos, who was the strongest Titan. During Ragnarok, several gods are shown owning foam fingers, which mimic Zeus' signature finger to the sky, and several god children are shown holding toys modeled after Heracles. This could imply that the Gods have a similar idea of celebrities to humans, with particularly well-known Gods getting merchandise made after them
Laws:
It is stated that the Gods have a constitution, called the Valhalla Constitution. This makes clear that in Heaven, deities and other beings have rights and laws that they must follow. The Gods also have courtrooms, meaning that criminals must be prosecuted in order to be convicted. However, as seen during Eve's trial, the Gods have prejudices against Humans, making the legal system very flawed.
Humans who consume the Forbidden Fruit from the tree in the Garden of Eden are banished from the garden.
Only the Chief Gods (also known as the Supreme Gods) can pass through the Bifröst freely. Anyone who is not a Chief God will be forbidden to return to Valhalla and is imprisoned in Helheim for all eternity.
Every 1000 years, the Gods must gather in a council to vote on whether or not Humanity should continue existing.
In accordance to the Article No. 62, Paragraph 15 of the Super Special Clause of the Valhalla Constitution, if the Gods decide to end Humanity, mankind has the right to challenge the Gods to a tournament of 13 one-on-one showdowns. If mankind wins the tournament, they will be allowed to live for the next 1000 years.
Technology:
Gods are far more technologically advanced than current human civilization. Even during Ancient Greece, the Gods had already managed to create phone-like devices. The Gods are also a lot more developed in the fields of biology and medicine than humankind, with deities such as Beelzebub being capable of creating artificial lifeforms.
Types of Gods:
Supreme Gods
"Supreme God" appears to be a title given to a deity that is far more powerful than the average. They usually are the leader or the supreme deity of their respective pantheons. However, some pantheons, such as the Greek Pantheon, have multiple Supreme Gods. Supreme Gods are usually rulers of important regions or realms and because of their position they have multiple benefits alongside heavy responsibilities. When the Gods are at war, its their duty to fight at the frontlines and lead their armies. They are also called Chief Gods.
Known Supreme Gods: Zeus, Hades, Shiva, Odin
Primordial Gods:
It is unknown what exactly a "Primordial God" is. However, from their name, it can be assumed that they are Gods that are far older than the average deity. Gaia and "Arkhé" are the only deities that have been referred to as primordial beings.

Demigods:
"Demigods" are half-God and half-Human deities. The difference between a demigod and a full God is very unclear. A demigod is not a Human who became a God, since Buddha is considered a full God (despite being born as a Human). Demigods are also not necessarily weaker than full Gods, since Heracles is more powerful than most Gods, despite being a demigod. The common characteristic among all demigods and what seems to separate them from the Gods is their inherent deep connection with Humanity.
Overall Abilities: Gods are by far the most powerful beings in existence. They were able to defeat all their enemies and assert themselves as the rulers of all the three realms (Heaven, Earth and Hell). It has been stated and shown that they are capable of causing massive destruction and influencing reality to a great extent: Creating life, evolving animals, flooding the Earth, destroying key elements of civilizations, creating an Ice Age and wiping out Humanity are some of the feats that the Gods have claimed to be capable of doing or have done it at some point in history. Some of the most powerful deities such as Zeus and Thor have showcased the ability to potentially destroy planets. However, this level of power is very rare among the Gods.
Divine Physiology: Most Gods have physical abilities far greater than most Humans. They are also immune to all attacks with man-made weapons, which also possibly includes nuclear weapons. However, they can still be harmed by Divine Weapons and by unarmed attacks from individuals with superhuman strength. Some Gods also have supernatural abilities, such as Thor's electrokinesis or Zerofuku's misfortune manipulation.
Semi-Immortality: The Gods appear to be unable to die due to old age. They also appear to be immune to the effects of time, where they stop aging upon reaching a certain age. However, they can still be killed by other means.
Divine Weapon Creation: Gods have the ability to forge Divine Weapons. These weapons are superior to all man-made weapons and are one of the main reasons for the Gods' tremendous power over Humanity.
Adamas and Zerofuku are original characters created for. Zerofuku has also not been confirmed to be associated with any known religion.
While he is a Philistine God, Beelzebub is also a major demon in some Abrahamic religions and can therefore be associated with both religions.
Benzaiten, Bishamonten and Daikokuten originate from Mahayana Buddhism; Fukurokuju, Hotei and Jurojin originate from Chinese Taoism; Ebisu originates from Japanese beliefs. However, the Seven Lucky Gods (as a group), comes from Japanese mythology (for this reason they are considered members of the Shinto Pantheon).
relationship:
Titans:
While the relationship between Gods and Titans is mostly unknown, it was shown that the two species had a fighting tournament before Ragnarok, known as the Titanomachy. Due to this fact, it can be assumed that the two species saw each other as rivals and enemies. However, the two species can work together. This was seen when the Titans decided to aid Adamas in his attempt to overthrow Zeus.
Giants:
As shown in Thor's flashback, the Gods feared the Giants and the Giants treated the Gods as a source of food. However, some Gods, such as Gaia, appear to be on friendly terms with the Giants.
Humans:
As their creators, the Gods looked down on Humanity while Humans lived in fear of the Gods. However, as Ragnarok goes on, the Gods are growing to respect Humanity whereas the Humans seem to be getting more and more daring in how they treat the deities.
Demons:
While not much is known about Demons in general, some of them (such as The Serpent) appear to be on friendly terms with the Gods. However, some Gods, such as Hades, have the duty to supervise the Demons, in order to prevent them from causing any trouble.
Angels:
They are the servants, guards and warriors of the Gods and also the angels are loyal and obedient to them.

entries.name: Demons
entries.content:
Demons are one of the existing species in the world of. They are unearthly beings that dwell in the underworld.
Demons are the creatures or beings that inhabit the netherworld. Similar to the gods, demons have a very humanoid appearance, being very similar to that of a human. Some also have been shown to possess non human traits, such as horns or wings. While not confirmed to be immortal like the gods, demons are still very powerful, to the point that they can be very dangerous in case they get out of control.
All demons shown so far appear to be inherently evil or malicious, acting almost purely by their instincts. However it has not been confirm that all demons are evil by nature.
Origins and History:
Their origins are not very clear. However, it is known that after the Titanomachy Tournament, Hades became the ruler of Helheim. This was done so that he could supervise the demons in order to prevent them from causing any trouble in the netherworld or going up to Midgard and causing chaos.
Culture:
Little is currently known about the organisation and society of Helheim. However from what is shown, hell appears to be a very violent place with little to no laws or order.
Abilities:
Demonic Physiology: Similar to the gods, Demons have physical abilities far greater than most humans. Some demons also have supernatural abilities, such as Hajun's veil of darkness.
