Hades sighed about how Beelzebub was such a bothersome fellow before admitting he liked how that sounded.
He then gave him the Staff of Apomyius since Beelzebub won't go down so easily with that before promising to see to Beelzebub's continued suffering and savage demise. Beelzebub asked Hades why he had any concern about him and Hades admitted it was because he was missing his younger brothers, who are quite bothersome, and Beelzebub reminded him of them. As he left, Beelzebub said that Hades was quite a bothersome God himself, much to Hades' confusion.
Adamas' Betrayal:
Upset over how Zeus became the ruler of Heaven, Adamas plotted a rebellion. To help, Adamas freed the remaining Titans and Giants and even bent the grisly Typhon to his will. Adamas also enlisted the help of Hermes, who convinced a number of the other 13 Gods of Olympus to defect, along with 49 members of Zeus' council.
To seal Zeus' fate, Adamas visited Poseidon's palace and tried to convince his younger brother to help him. However, Poseidon was only disappointed and cold-heartedly stated that Adamas defiled everything the Gods stood for. An angered Adamas tried to attack Poseidon but Poseidon grievously injured him with just one thrust of his trident. He then threw Adamas' body aside and left.
Having watched the whole ordeal secretly, Hermes would soon contact Hades and inform him on what happened to Adamas. To save Adamas' life, Hades ordered Hermes to take him to Beelzebub, who proceeded to heal Adamas by reconstructing his body into a cyborg. Since Poseidon had Adamas' name erased from history, he continued to live under a different name, Adamantine, in Helheim.
Relationships:
Poseidon:
Out of all of his brothers, Poseidon seemed to be the one Hades cared the most about. The two had a good relationship, with Hades not minding Poseidon's harsh demeanor and talking to him casually despite his fearsome reputation. He was shocked when Poseidon called him his brother, noting that was the first time he had ever done so.
During Ragnarok, Poseidon's death was the reason Hades left Helheim and came up to Valhalla to join the Gods' roster. Hades merged Poseidon's trident with his own bident and fought Qin Shi Huang in memory of his late brother and the promise he made with him; that he'd never lose to anyone when fighting for his family. Hades' fighting style bore a striking resemblance to Poseidon's, as well as his singing and mannerisms after cutting himself open. Poseidon's outstretched hand was also the last thing Hades saw before his death.
Adamas:
Hades was on good terms with Adamas, despite his wanting to overthrow Zeus. Adamas held great love and respect for Hades, and even felt comfortable working with him in Helheim. While the two never interacted directly in the series, Hades was the one who ordered Hermes to save Adamas, and was the one who contacted Beelzebub to revive him. Hades also apologized to Adamas before his death.
Zeus:
Hades and Zeus had a good relationship, though seemingly not one as close as Hades had with Poseidon. The two got along well and Hades held unconditional love for his youngest brother just like the rest of his family. Hades apologized to Zeus before his death.
Beelzebub:
Hades was good friends with Beelzebub. Despite the latter's fearsome reputation and murdering of his friends, Hades still pitied him and decided to help Beelzebub live a fulfilling life. He initially listened to Beelzebub's request to kill him, but before delivering the final blow, he decided against it after hearing about Lilith's curse. He urged Beelzebub to search himself for the meaning of her prayer, and that if he still wanted to die, he would be waiting. When Beelzebub eventually did return, Hades was amused by his new approach to life: to live as horribly and corruptly as possible so that he would receive an equally painful death. He provided Beelzebub with the Staff of Apomyius, hoping that the now much stronger Beelzebub would have a much harder time dying. When asked by Beelzebub why he cared about him so much, Hades stated that he had three bothersome younger brothers, and just when he began to miss them, Beelzebub had wandered into his palace.
Hades outlawed the use of Original Sin of the Netherworld — No. 0: Chaos, due to the destruction it caused and due to the effects it had on Beelzebub. When Adamas was gravely injured by Poseidon, Hades contacted Beelzebub to save his brother, showing the trust he had in him. Hades' death also had a large impact on Beelzebub, as he'd been his only friend after his other friends and lover were killed by his Demonic Destrudo.
Ares and Hermes:
Hades was on good terms with Ares and Hermes. He interacted very little with Hermes, but he seemed to tolerate him and value his presence. Hades often made fun of Ares, and seemed to scare the God of War too. However, Ares still looked up to his uncle and found him to be the most reliable God.

entries.name: Apollo
entries.content:
Apollo is a prominent deity within the Greek Pantheon. He is known as the "Sun God" (太陽神, Taiyō-Shin) and is a part of the Twelve Gods of Olympus. He is also known by the title of "Phoebus" (ポイボス, Poibosu) and is considered to be the "Boxing God" (ボクシングの神, Bokushingu no Kami).
Through his own effort, Apollo has earned himself a number of distinguished titles, such as the "God of Philosophy" (哲学の神, Tetsugaku no Kami), the "God of Poetry" (詩歌の神, Shiika no Kami), the "God of Medicine" (医学の神, Igaku no Kami), the "God of Archery" (弓の神, Yumi no Kami), the "God of Music" (音楽の神, Ongaku no Kami) and the "God of Prophecy" (予言の神, Yogen no Kami), being praised as the most talented God.
SPECIES: God
AGE: Eons
GENDER: Male
PANTHEON: Greek Pantheon
ORIGIN: Unknown (Heaven, possibly)
RELATIVES: Artemis (Twin sister)
Zeus(father)
Appearance:
Apollo is an attractive man with flowing long light pink hair that reaches down to his torso and a body of good physique.
Like many of the Gods of the Greek Pantheon, he wears items related to Greece such as a laurel wreath, buskin sandals and toga. The toga though has elements of clothing more akin to a kimono such a sash around his torso (Obi) and flower designs on the outside of the chest area with it being opened to show his chest. He is decorated with jewelry with him wearing a necklace extending down his chest that resemble the sun and its rays, a chain that is a part of his sash and a decorated chain around his right leg. Underneath his Divine Weapon, he wears black gloves that only cover his thumbs, index and middle fingers, leaving his ring fingers and pinkies, and the area around them, exposed.
Personality:
Apollo appears to be an extremely narcissistic individual, who cares a lot about beauty, when it comes to himself and even others. When he had heard news of the deaths of other Greek Gods in Ragnarok, his first reaction wasn't to mourn them but rather, wish he could've been there to see their deaths as they must've looked beautiful when they died. In addition to being narcissistic, Apollo looks down on anyone who doesn't fit his own standards of what is beautiful. This is especially in the case of Humans such as at the start of the ninth round: when Leonidas leapt in before Heimdall could even finish saying "Fight!", Apollo criticised him for being like a wild beast, considering him less than a Human.
Apollo's narcissistic nature has also made him have a flare for the dramatic, always doing grandiose and expressive poses. This was first demonstrated when he was in the bath and posing for each grand line, not caring if he was nude or not. This did not dim down in battle, with him outright mocking Leonidas with his expressions, words and poses.
Apollo strongly believes that what makes a person beautiful is not what their outward appearance looks like – it's whether or not that person truly knows themself. He thinks that those aren't beautiful are those who rest on the laurels of their good fortune and do nothing more while those that are beautiful are those who know their own weaknesses and don't fear changing themselves.
Abilities:
Overall Abilities: Narcissism aside, Apollo is a formidable God in combat, thanks to his extreme reflexes and speed that make him nearly impossible to hit. Combined with his natural talent in boxing, Apollo can counter any attack without losing momentum or breath. So much so, he could put fighters like Leonidas on the ropes where even Leonidas' Völundr could not surprise the God enough to let his guard completely down.
Physical Abilities:
Godly Speed & Reflexes: Apollo had demonstrated not only speed to that of a God or Human fighter, but possibly speed that surpasses others. This was demonstrated when an angry Ares, the God of War, tried to slug the Sun God for his insolence while he was in the nude, with Apollo effortlessly dodging and even throwing the God of War into the water. Apollo can even quickly adapt to sudden attacks, with him able to dodge many of Leonidas' surprise attacks despite never seeing them until that moment.
Godly Endurance & Stamina: Apollo has great resistance and can withstand very strong and painful blows. When Leonidas managed to hit Apollo with Phalanx Nemesis, he received the blow directly to his face and hit the ground so hard that he bounced off it and fell back to the ground face-first. Although it took him a while to get up, it didn't take him long, and his reaction was one of happiness and joy, fully accepting the unsightly wound on his face with pride.
Mental Abilities:
Self-Knowledge: Apollo was born as an ordinary and mediocre god, but thanks to his desire to be better, he managed to achieve all his titles, skills and competencies through pure hard work and effort. His knowledge of himself led him to improve and become one of the 12 Gods of Olympus. He is the first natural God who has accepted that he is weak and strived to be the strongest.
Fighting Abilities:
Master Boxer: Apollo has shown immense skill in boxing, evident by his ability to dodge Leonidas' quick attacks, while also being able to quickly strike back.
Master Archer: Apollo has been classified as a very skilled archer, during his life he has trained and practiced a lot to become "God of Archery", in addition to that he himself has been able to kill several Giants, and destroy the defenses of Argos during the Gigantomachy, and also for the fact of wounding Leonidas numerous times.
Supernatural Abilities:
Semi-immortality: As a God, Apollo is incapable of dying due to old age.
Divine Physiology: As a God, Apollo possesses physical abilities far greater than any ordinary Human. His body cannot be harmed by mortal weapons; however, he can still be harmed by unarmed attacks from individuals with superhuman strength and Divine Weapons.
Photokinesis: As the God of the Sun, Apollo can produce and control light. He can manipulate and craft the light into fine and durable threads for combat that can block Volundr-level attacks with ease.
Matter Manipulation: Thanks to his threads of light that he can create, Apollo can manipulate and weave them to create any weapon or object he needs. This will open up an infinite number of possibilities such as a Shield, a Lyre, Boxing Gloves, a Bow, etc.
Expectations-Induced Enhancement: Apollo can enhance his physical, mental and supernatural abilities based on the expectations and criticism of others, whether allies or enemies. This was seen when he activated his strongest form because of all the comments from the stands. It is a power that Zeus himself cannot define, since it is not tied to any type of logic or common sense. The more the public's emotion, the more affinity Apolo will have.
Techniques:
Phoebus' Lyre (The Shimmering Harp) (光輝きて堅琴ポイボス・ライアー, Poibosu Raiā): Apollo creates a pair of hands out of his threads and places his own hands into them, which transforms the Threads of Artemis into a pair of boxing bracers with pronounced wristbands and studded knuckles. These pair of bracers enhance Apollo's close-range boxing abilities.
The Sun Shall Never Set on Me (Embrace of the Eternal Midnight Sun) (白夜の抱擁オレ様という太陽は沈まない, Oresama to iu Taiyō wa Shizumanai): Apollo's strongest battle mode. A power that defies all logic and common sense, Apollo can actually get stronger the more that he lives up to the expectations of those around him, whether they be an ally or an enemy. When this happens, Apollo emits a large amount of light from his body.
Artemis Elenchos (Shining Domination) (光り輝く支配アルテミス・エレンコス, Arutemisu Erenkosu): Apollo wraps his threads around his opponent's limb to immobilise their movement.
Apollo Epicurious (Golden Arrows of the Shining Meteor) (輝ける流星の黄金矢アポロン・エピクリオス, Aporon Epikuriosu): Apollo launches a large wave of his light arrows at his opponent to overwhelm them.
Argyrotoxos (Soul-Piercing Silver Arrow) (魂を射抜し銀矢アリュギュロトクソス, Aryugyurotokusosu): If Apollo cannot draw his bow anymore, he can give the bow back to the statue. The statue will then deform the bow back into threads and form a very thick rope between its hands. Afterwards, the statue drops its hands to the ground and Apollo leans back on the rope while digging his feet really hard into the ground, drawing himself back like an arrow. Once he pulls his right fist back in preparation for a punch, Apollo lifts his feet up from the ground and is sent flying towards his opponent. While flying forward, Apollo's right fist hardens the light energy that is around it, creating an arrow covering it. This attack was powerful enough to destroy Leonidas' Völundr and deal a fatal blow through his body in the final moments of Round 9, though the arrow was broken on impact with the shield.
Equipment:
Threads of Artemis (アルテミスの糸, Arutemisu no Ito): A set of golden gauntlets with a dark blue underside, three small studs on each knuckle, and small holes above each fingertip. Upon Apollo producing light from his fingertips, they transform into threads that he can use for defensive or offensive purposes.
Moonlight of Artemis (アルテミスの月影, Arutemisu no Tsukikage): Apollo's Threads of Artemis disappear from his hands and right after, a large shadow extends out behind him. A giant statue of Artemis then appears from the shadow, equipped with Apollo's Divine Weapon. The statue weaves the threads it produces to make a giant golden bow, its length being twice as tall as Apollo is. Apollo can use the bow to fire arrows of light, that are invisible when fired because they move at light speed. Because of how fast the arrows are, they are known as the fastest attack in Valhalla and Zeus believes no-one other than himself can defend against them.
Gigantomachy:
Along with all the other Greek Gods, Apollo took part in the Gigantomachy against Gaia and the Giants. It is noted by Hermes that this war was the last time Apollo shined greatly before the ninth round of Ragnarok. Zeus has stated that Apollo used his golden bow against the Giants during this war and that the Giants could do nothing against his arrows of light.
During the time of Ancient Greece on Earth, a serpent-like monster called Python was driven out of Valhalla for his hideous appearance. Shunned by the Humans as well, Python took out his frustration on them by constantly terrorizing the village of Delphi. During one of his rampages, Ares sent his Divine Honor Guard to stop him but Python easily dealt with them. After hearing of this, the next day, Apollo went down to Earth and confronted Python at his hideout, wanting to meet Ares' expectations by defeating Python by himself, though Ares never asked him to.
Python was excited to see Apollo as he perceived the God to be the complete opposite of himself. Thus, Python wanted to rip his face to shreds. Python charged forward but Apollo leapt in and punched Python squarely in the face. Apollo decided this was his win and Python found himself unable to get up, from just one punch. Not wanting to give up, Python shouted about how he hasn't lost yet and Apollo found that attitude great, telling Python that they shall continue their fight tomorrow. Apollo went to sleep in Python's bed and ordered him to find somewhere else to sleep.
For the next several days, Apollo fought Python, defeating him in one punch every time. During one rainy day, Apollo got curious and asked Python why he continued to fight him. Python divulged to Apollo how he was despised and oppressed because of an appearance he didn't even ask for. The serpent cried and insisted that he couldn't stomach the thought of losing to Apollo, who seemed to have been blessed with everything from birth. When Python expressed his unwillingness to give up, Apollo said he was beautiful.[9] Python thought Apollo was making fun of him but Apollo clarified that he wasn't referring to Python's appearance; rather he found Python's soul beautiful.
He explained to Python that he could understand him because he was the same. Apollo was originally a mediocre God but he worked hard and became recognized through effort alone, to the point where he was able to join the ranks of the Twelve Gods of Olympus. Apollo told Python that the ones who aren't beautiful to him are those who are satisfied with where they are while those who are beautiful, are those who know they aren't enough and don't fear changing themselves for the better. Finally understanding, Python then began crying over how he'd hurt so many people, but Apollo didn't hold it against him as he was just defending himself. Apollo decided to go back to Valhalla and Python shouted about how he still hasn't lost, causing Apollo to remark on how that's beauty.
After Apollo left, Python stopped terrorizing Delphi and instead, built a temple dedicated to Apollo, engraving it with the words, "Know Thyself."
